summary: Retapamulin is the first pleuromutilin antibacterial approved for topical human use, indicated for the topical treatment of impetigo due to Staphylococcus aureus (methicillin-susceptible isolates only) or Streptococcus pyogenes. It is supplied as a 1% ointment applied as a thin layer to the affected area twice daily for 5 days. It is for topical use only (not for oral, ophthalmic, intranasal, or intravaginal use) and is not intended for lesions known or suspected to be caused by MRSA, against which it lacked adequate efficacy. Systemic absorption after topical application is low, so adverse effects are mainly local (application-site irritation). Prolonged use may cause overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms.
indications: Topical treatment of impetigo due to Staphylococcus aureus (methicillin-susceptible isolates only) or Streptococcus pyogenes in adults and pediatric patients (per labeling, 9 months of age and older)

moa: Retapamulin is a semisynthetic pleuromutilin antibacterial. It inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding at a unique site on the 50S ribosomal subunit (domain V of 23S rRNA, at the peptidyl transferase center), thereby interfering with peptide bond formation and ribosomal P-site interactions. Because of this distinct binding site, target-specific cross-resistance with other antibacterial classes is generally absent.

preg: There are limited data on retapamulin use in pregnant women. Because systemic absorption after topical application is low, fetal exposure is expected to be minimal. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether retapamulin is excreted in human milk; given negligible systemic absorption, exposure to a breastfed infant is expected to be minimal. Use with caution in nursing mothers and avoid applying directly to the breast/nipple area while breastfeeding.
renal: No systemic dosage adjustment is expected for renal impairment because retapamulin is a topical agent with negligible systemic absorption.
hepatic: No systemic dosage adjustment is expected for hepatic impairment given negligible systemic absorption after topical use.

major: No clinically significant systemic drug interactions are expected with topical use
moderate: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole) could theoretically raise the very low systemic retapamulin levels - not clinically significant with recommended topical use
minor: Other topical products applied to the same area (no formal data)

serious: Overgrowth of nonsusceptible bacteria or fungi with prolonged use
rare: Worsening of the underlying infection (if pathogen not susceptible)
emergency: Serious allergic reaction (e.g., severe rash, swelling, difficulty breathing)

pearls: First topical pleuromutilin antibacterial; binds the 50S ribosomal peptidyl transferase center - distinct site with little cross-resistance
For impetigo due to MSSA or S. pyogenes - NOT effective against MRSA (do not use for suspected MRSA)
Topical use only; negligible systemic absorption means minimal systemic toxicity and interactions
Standard course is twice daily for 5 days; treated area limited (up to 100 cm2 in adults)
missed: If an application is missed, apply it as soon as remembered, then continue the twice-daily schedule. Do not apply extra ointment to make up for a missed application. Complete the full 5-day course as directed.
overdose: Any sign or symptom of overdose, whether topical or by accidental ingestion, should be treated symptomatically. There is no specific antidote. Given low systemic absorption, serious systemic toxicity from topical overuse is unlikely.
